provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.4 (Windows Secondary WebView Load & Presentation Rendering Reliability) - rebuilt to package: (1) converting the two Tauri commands that create the presentation display window (display_presentation, open_presentation_display) from synchronous to async fn, per a documented Tauri/WRY Windows-specific deadlock in WebviewWindowBuilder::new/build when called from a synchronous command (https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/583, cited directly in the vendored Tauri 2.11.5 crate's own doc comments) - a window frame can appear while the WebView2 control inside it deadlocks before ever navigating, producing WebView2's own default white background rather than this app's CSS, which matches the operator's exact real Windows evidence; and (2) additive diagnostic logging covering the previously-uncovered page-load and React-branch-selection boundaries
provenance.buildEnvironment: cross-compiled from Linux using rustup target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, gcc-mingw-w64, and nsis (makensis) - identical toolchain to every prior phase, see docs/phase-3-4-windows-pilot.md for the original toolchain setup and docs/phase-3-8-4-presentation-display-rendering.md for what changed this phase
provenance.note: This artifact supersedes the Phase 3.8.3 installer (previously SHA-256 f1df6631da8f4a13b586b28da9c9a6da883d253d8f56afc22474956aab753d7a) because this phase modified apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/presentation_display.rs (adds an on_page_load handler logging PageLoadEvent::Started/Finished + URL), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs (display_presentation and open_presentation_display changed from pub fn to pub async fn - names/parameters/return types unchanged), apps/desktop/src/main.tsx (module-scope branch-selection diagnostic + display-scoped window.onerror/unhandledrejection handler), apps/desktop/src/components/PresentationDisplay.tsx (uses the new shared presentationDiagnostics.ts helper), and added apps/desktop/src/components/presentationDiagnostics.ts (the shared logCheckpoint implementation, extracted so main.tsx and PresentationDisplay.tsx share one implementation). Zero new database migrations, zero renderer changes, zero Bible/intelligence engine changes, zero event contract changes, zero capability changes, zero Tauri command signature changes - see docs/phase-3-8-4-presentation-display-rendering.md for the full architectural-safety diff. This is a freshly compiled build (`cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` via `tauri build`), not a copy of a prior artifact.

releaseCandidateStatement: This is the Phase 3.8.4 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Windows Secondary WebView Load & Presentation Rendering Reliability). It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication. See docs/phase-3-8-4-presentation-display-rendering.md for the full PASS/HOLD breakdown and final gate.
physicalHardwareStatement: Physical hardware qualification has NOT been performed in the build environment. This installer has not been installed, launched, or tested on any real Windows machine. No real microphone, no real Whisper transcription, no real second display/projector, no real WebView2 runtime, and no real human operator workflow has been exercised against this build. Xvfb, simulated audio, virtual displays, automated tests, and cross-compilation success are Environment A/B evidence only and are never substituted for Environment C (real hardware) evidence anywhere in this project's documentation. The operator's own Phase 3.8.3 Windows testing (which reported the white-display symptom this phase investigates) is real Environment C usage of the PRIOR (Phase 3.8.3) build, not of this rebuilt artifact - per this phase's own explicit instruction, that prior test is never converted into PASS evidence for this rebuild. The applied async-command fix is strongly supported by first-party Tauri documentation matching this codebase's exact calling pattern and platform, but it has not been confirmed by direct reproduction on Windows because no physical Windows machine or WebView2 runtime is available in this container.
githubReleaseStatus: NOT CONFIGURED - no .github/workflows directory exists in this repository, and no GitHub Release has been created for this artifact. This installer is available only via this repository's working tree (release/windows/), not via GitHub Releases or any CI/CD pipeline.
obtainingWithoutDeveloperTooling: The file at release/windows/Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe can be copied/transferred directly (e.g. via a git clone of this repository, a direct file download, or a USB drive) to the target Windows machine and run there. Running the installer on Windows requires none of: Claude Code, Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, or the CIP source tree - only the .exe file itself.
knownLimitations: UNSIGNED release candidate - Windows SmartScreen will show an 'unknown publisher' warning on first run
Cross-compiled from Linux, never launch-tested on real Windows hardware - Environment C remains not performed for THIS rebuilt artifact

The async-command fix is strongly supported by first-party Tauri/WRY documentation citing the exact calling pattern this codebase used, not a confirmed root cause - it could not be directly reproduced or confirmed in this environment (no physical Windows machine, no WebView2 runtime available here)

The diagnostic logging (14 checkpoints from Phase 3.8.3, plus page-load and branch-selection checkpoints added this phase) is temporary, development-only instrumentation intended to be read directly from the log file (RUST_LOG is not required - checkpoints log at Info level) if the display is still white/blank after this fix on real Windows hardware; it is not a permanent feature and should be removed once the real root cause is confirmed

Music Library is legitimately empty in a production build - no licensed production song dataset exists in this repository; Service Replay's default flow does not exercise Music Intelligence for this reason

The ground-up visual/UX redesign described aspirationally in the original Phase 3.8 spec was deliberately not attempted this phase either - scope remained limited to the specific rendering defect the operator reported
See docs/phase-3-8-4-presentation-display-rendering.md and pilot-evidence/3.8.4/ for the full Environment A/B/C evidence breakdown
